title: Balanced finite-context bandits compared with all lookup-table policies
summary: Each round first reveals a discrete context. The learner then selects an arm and observes its loss. The comparator is any fixed mapping from contexts to arms. Context occurrence counts are balanced as required by the model.

description_paragraphs: Each round first reveals a discrete context. The learner then selects an arm and observes its loss. The comparator is any fixed mapping from contexts to arms. Context occurrence counts are balanced as required by the model.

model.instance: The public context sequence is the balanced cycle c_t=1+((t-1) mod S), with S dividing T. The environment fixes each loss vector ell_t in [0,1]^K in advance. The learner observes the context before selecting an arm and sees only the selected loss.

assumptions.scope: The objects, time horizon, and variable blocks explicitly declared here; none is inherited from another specification.
assumptions.description: Each ℓ_t lies in [0,1]^K, and the sequence is precommitted.

assumptions.scope: The objects, time horizon, and variable blocks explicitly declared here; none is inherited from another specification.
assumptions.description: Every context appears exactly $T/S$ times. The schedule is public and independent of learner actions.

model.parameter_domain_description: K: $K\in\mathbb N,\ K\ge2$ (public); S: $S\in\mathbb N,\ S\ge1,\ S\mid T$ (public); T: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public)
interaction_timing: The environment fixes the loss sequence; the balanced cyclic context schedule is public.
Select $a_t$ from the current $c_t$ and the history.
model.adversary_information: The environment fixes the complete loss sequence before interaction. It may know the algorithm and public parameters but cannot depend on the learner's private seed. This is an oblivious environment; nonanticipation describes the learner's causal information and does not extend the specification to a history-adaptive adversary.
unresolved_applicability: General context sequences, restricted policy classes, regression oracles, and stochastic realizable models are not covered by this balanced tabular specification.
description_paragraphs: The context schedule $c_{1:T}$ is public and balanced, with each context appearing $T/S$ times. Contexts are neither random nor adversarially selected during the run.
The current hidden loss vector $\ell_t$ lies in [0,1]^K and is fixed in advance.
The comparator is the best fixed policy $\pi:[S]\to[K]$ in hindsight, assigning one arm to each context, possibly different arms across contexts.
Require $K\ge2$, $S,T\ge1$, and $S\mid T$, with actual action $a_t\in[K]$.

operations.query_signature: The input-output sequence is $c_t\longrightarrow a_t\in[K]$. The declared protocol fixes timing and visible information.
operations.order_convention: order is relative to the current member f_t(x), f(x), or sample F(x;ξ_t) of the named indexed function family and only with respect to x; finite feedback interfaces have no derivative order

feedback_quality.description: The context is revealed before a_t is submitted, and the full cyclic schedule is public from the outset. Losses are hidden before selection, and only the chosen arm's scalar loss is returned afterward. No counterfactual loss for another context or second-arm feedback in the same round is available.

operations.coupling: The context is revealed before a_t is submitted, and the full cyclic schedule is public from the outset. Losses are hidden before selection, and only the chosen arm's scalar loss is returned afterward. No counterfactual loss for another context or second-arm feedback in the same round is available.
operations.index_control: The learner selects feasible actions and any probes permitted by the specification. The environment determines current losses, outcomes, or fresh samples. The learner cannot select future rounds.
operations.access_schedule: Interaction follows the sequence in registry.protocols. Current loss feedback is available only after the action is submitted. Any pre-action disclosure of context or advice is specified separately.

public_inputs: A complete balanced cyclic context schedule, with S dividing T.
auxiliary_interfaces: No additional access to hidden losses, means, or gradients is available. Projection, sampling, and internal optimization over public domains may have separately recorded computation costs; they are not free loss oracles.
oracle.query_domain_description: The action set is $[K]$, and the current context $c_t\in[S]$ is revealed before acting.
description_paragraphs: Context before the action; selected-arm loss after the action:

$$
c_t\ \longrightarrow\ a_t\in[K]\ \longmapsto\ Y_t=\ell_t(a_t)
$$
The current context is public before action $a_t$. The full cyclic schedule is also a public input.
Losses are hidden before selection; only one scalar for the selected arm is returned afterward.
There is no counterfactual loss feedback for other contexts or second-arm feedback within a round.
Public inputs: K, T, S, and the complete balanced cyclic context schedule, with S dividing T.

output.feasibility: Every loss-bearing action must belong to the action domain. The final output retains the complete action trajectory.
output.allowed_postprocessing: Any measurable computation on received feedback is allowed. No native observation may be added after the budget is exhausted or the algorithm stops.
output.certificate_requirement: Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.
description_paragraphs: The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. Retrospective averages or convex combinations cannot replace actions that have already incurred loss. No additional optimal value or certificate is required.

metric.normalization: Use the cumulative quantity over T rounds without dividing by T. Preserve the displayed order of probability or expectation.
metric.finiteness_conditions: Both cumulative losses lie in [0,T], so their difference on each execution path lies in [-T,T].
description_paragraphs:
$$
c_t=1+((t-1)\bmod S),\quad R_T=\sum_t\ell_t(a_t)-\min_{\pi:[S]\to[K]}\sum_t\ell_t(\pi(c_t))
$$

components.description: Sequential online rounds; only information permitted by the protocol is visible in each round.
Each round reveals one context identifier and one selected-arm loss, for T arm-feedback observations in total.

resource.budget_semantics: There are T sequential interaction rounds. Native feedback count is determined by the per-round protocol and is not an independent budget to minimize.
resource.scalarization: Retain the native objective and complete resource vector. At fixed $T$, compare cumulative regret. Best-arm-identification stopping times and error probabilities use their own task-specific criteria.
resource.setup_cost: Only declared public inputs may be read. Hidden losses, means, or samples cannot be accessed in advance or outside the $T$ rounds or $\tau$ samples.
resource.online_cost: Run a separate bandit algorithm for each of the S contexts, updating only the state of the current context each round. This uses O(SK) arm statistics and realizes the bound without enumerating K^S policies.
resource.amortization_scope: The algorithm runs on one environment. Charged feedback cannot be reused across independent instances.
resource.precision_model: Observations and internal arithmetic use the exact-real model. No bit-complexity claim follows.
description_paragraphs: Each round reveals one context identifier and one selected-arm loss, for T arm-feedback observations in total.
Run a separate bandit algorithm for each of S contexts and update only the current context's state each round.
The upper bound can be implemented with $O(SK)$ arm statistics, without enumerating all $K^S$ comparator policies. This witness's memory use is distinct from the unrestricted algorithm class.

Information calls, arithmetic, communication rounds, and memory are measured separately. Exact real internal computation is excluded from information complexity unless explicitly charged. This does not imply a bit-complexity bound.

algorithms.randomization: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.
algorithms.adaptivity: The action and every probe in a round may depend only on previous-round feedback, public inputs, any context or advice already revealed that round, and private randomness. They may not use unrevealed current losses or samples.
restrictions: All measurable causal policies satisfying the declared information timing and feasible domain are allowed, without extra span, iteration-form, or polynomial-time restrictions.
algorithms.internal_computation: Arbitrary measurable computation with exact real arithmetic is permitted; feedback complexity does not imply arithmetic or bit complexity. Run a separate bandit algorithm for each of $S$ contexts, updating only the current context. The implementation uses $O(SK)$ arm statistics and does not enumerate $K^S$ policies.
algorithms.parallelism: Interaction proceeds in sequential time rounds. A two-point evaluation is one pair of same-round responses only where explicitly permitted; it is not equivalent to two independent rounds.
description_paragraphs: All measurable causal randomized policies respecting the stated timing are allowed. The private seed is independent of the fixed instance and future samples. Apart from explicit feedback, output, and budget requirements, there are no restrictions on linear spans, iteration form, internal arithmetic, memory, or communication.

guarantees.complete_expression: The native objective is $\inf_{\mathcal A}\sup_{\ell_{1:T}}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}[R_T]$.
aggregation_order: First take the infimum over complete nonanticipating learning policies using only public inputs.
Then take the supremum over instances fixed before interaction that satisfy the stated model.
Expectation includes learner randomness and, when present, observation noise or random samples.
The objective fixes the comparator. Per-round optimal actions, a fixed action, and a sample-path optimum are not interchangeable.
guarantees.quantifier_order: One learning algorithm must apply to every instance in the declared class. It may use public inputs only, not hidden instance parameters.
guarantees.time_uniformity: The horizon T is fixed and public. The guarantee holds for that T; it does not automatically give an anytime result or a simultaneous high-probability statement for all T.
description_paragraphs:
$$
\inf_{\mathcal{A}}\sup_{\ell_{1:T}}\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{A}}[R_T]
$$

Choose one algorithm using public inputs before taking the worst case over all admissible instances. Expectation covers the algorithm's private randomness and the observation randomness specified by the model. Comparator choice and the order of summation, minimization, and expectation follow the displayed formula.

quantities.expression: R*_T = inf_{A in admissible nonanticipating randomized learners} sup_{I in declared model} E_A,I[sum_t ℓ_t(a_t)−min_{π:[S]→[K]}sum_t ℓ_t(π(c_t))].
quantities.analysis_scope: Compare only this specification and the listed parameter regions.
quantities.expression_latex: \begin{aligned}\mathcal R_T^*&=\inf_{\mathcal A}\sup_{\ell_{1:T}\in([0,1]^K)^T}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}[R_T],\\ R_T&=\sum_{t=1}^T\ell_t(a_t)-\min_{\pi:[S]\to[K]}\sum_{t=1}^T\ell_t(\pi(c_t)),\\ c_t&=1+((t-1)\bmod S),\qquad S\mid T.\end{aligned}

bounds.derivation: Each context occurs $T/S$ times. Running Tsallis-INF separately for each context gives the bound $4\sqrt{KT/S}+1$ per context. The best context-to-arm mapping decomposes by context, so the regrets of the $S$ independent algorithm states can be summed.

bounds.derivation: Each context appears $n=T/S\ge K$ times. Choose hard optimal arms independently across contexts so other-context observations reveal no information about that identity. Summing block lower bounds gives $0.04S\sqrt{Kn}$. Averaging over the loss table sampled in advance yields an oblivious sequence lower bound.

evidence.supports: Supports the stated results and explicit reductions: $\mathcal{R}_T^*\le4\sqrt{KST}+S$. Each bound retains its own model, feedback, parameter region, and quantifiers.
notes: Tsallis-INF has adversarial bandit pseudo-regret at most $4\sqrt{KT}+1$. For a deterministic loss sequence fixed before interaction, this equals expected realized external regret.

evidence.supports: The source supports $\mathcal{R}_T^*\ge0.04\sqrt{KST}$ and the stated reductions, subject to each atomic claim's model, feedback, parameter region, and quantifiers.
notes: Use only the K-armed bandit branch with source sampling budget $m_{\mathrm{src}}=T$. In context-block reductions each block uses its own length. Bernoulli hard instances and Yao's principle give the randomized-learner lower bound.
